beats.t: A large sheet of paper went up on Moka's underground kitchen wall. Crooked letters at the top read: Operation Noon Concert.
Right, meeting starts now. Objective: raise the sun to noon.
First pig I've seen plan an operation from one line of a fairy tale.
You're the one who brought up that fairy tale.
We need three things. A high stage, people to sing together, and the courage to make the first sound.
The stage should be the highest place on the island. Where the black feather fell.
The Sundial Stage. Performances used to happen there every noon. Now it's a crow's nest.
I'll gather people. I'm good at promotion.
How do you promote a singing performance on an island where singing's banned?
Don't call it singing. Free skewers at noon. Everyone will come.
Who's grilling those skewers?
Now, which otter grills the best skewers on this island?
The pig whose voice turns into fire is handling promotion.
I'll control that. Probably.
Then the last part. Who makes the first sound?
Yeoni and Yeongnyangi looked at Moka together. Still holding his ladle, Moka backed away.
Why are you looking at me?
Now, which otter has the best rhythm on this island?
I told you, it's a recipe!
Read the recipe at noon. Loud enough to carry.
...So the cat makes jokes too.
Not a joke.
Yeoni headed to the gray market. Gathering people meant meeting people first.
The market remained quiet. But a small sound came from an alley entrance. Tap, tap-tap. Chopsticks tapping a wooden box.
A sound? Someone hasn't been stamped?
A boy of about ten sat before the box. The backs of his hands were clean. No stamps. He saw Yeoni and hid the chopsticks behind his back.
Don't hide them. I'm not an inspector. As you can see, I'm a pig.
The child watched Yeoni for a while, then gave a little smile. He tapped the box again. Tap, tap-tap, tap.
Nice rhythm. You've played drums before, haven't you?
He nodded. Then suddenly tilted his head, looking unable to remember when.
What's your name?
His mouth opened, then closed. Opened again. No name came out.
It's okay. If you can't remember, tell me later.
Child, what do your mother or friends call you?
He shrugged, looking puzzled that such an easy question had no answer.
He tried writing something on the box with a finger. Drew the first stroke and stopped. He did not know where the second should go.
Yeoni, look at his wrist.
A gold-thread mark encircled the child's wrist. A fine scar, as though a thread had been tied there and cut. A little gold still remained.
The mark of a debt-binding thread being cut. But his name was cut away with it.
I think I know who did that.
Yeoni remembered the strand of gold on the underground stage's floor. The same color.
Then I'll call you something for now. Captain Drum. How's that?
His eyes widened. Then he struck the box with his loudest beat. Tap, tap, boom.
That means you like it, right? Captain Drum, perform with us at noon.
On the seaside hill, Yeongnyangi sat on a rock and began the lesson. His students: one pig, one otter, one Captain Drum.
Two ways to use fire. Eating God and Hurting Officer.
Oh, finally unlocking the skill tree?
No tree. Only skewers.
Yeongnyangi signaled Moka. Moka placed six skewers on the grill.
Eating God first. Send fire to the skewers. Without anger. Think: become delicious.
Become delicious.
Yeoni extended a hoof toward the grill. Nothing. Tried again. One skewer warmed slightly.
Lukewarm. Serve that to a customer and it's one star.
You know you're setting my heart on fire right now?
All six skewers burst into flame at once. In an instant, they were charcoal.
My skewers!
That is Hurting Officer.
Uh, sorry. I got angry and it shot out.
The same fire. Only where your heart is looking differs. Again.
Six more skewers went on. Yeoni closed their eyes and imagined Grandmother's cart. The grandmother who gave two skewers to customers who could not sing.
Soy sauce hissed on the grill. The skewers browned evenly. Moka picked one up and tasted it.
...Four stars.
Four? Why not five?
Five belongs to Grandma. Don't get ambitious.
Now Hurting Officer. It is a blade. A blade must be used narrowly. Cut only that rope.
Yeongnyangi indicated a rope hanging from a rock's edge. An empty pot dangled from it.
Cut it with words, right? One phrase?
The shortest, most precise words.
Break free!
Two flaming words flew out. They chipped the rock beside the rope, knocked the pot away, and fell into the sea. The rope was untouched.
That was Grandma's pot!
Far too many family heirlooms are dying today.
Yeoni shouted ten more times. On the ninth, the rope broke. Captain Drum tapped his box. Boom, boom.
There. Remember that feeling.
Yeongnyangi staggered briefly as he stood, when he put weight on his right forepaw. He sat down again with an unconcerned face.
Yeongnyangi, is your leg asleep?
Cats' legs fall asleep after sitting too long too.
How old is this cat, anyway?
Do not ask.
A grandpa cat.
I said, do not ask.
My turn now. Practice.
Ooh, recipe-recital rehearsal!
Moka climbed onto the rock. Pig, cat, and child looked up at him. He opened his mouth.
Nothing came out. It was not a stamp. Moka's hands bore none.
...Close your eyes. All of you.
You can't even with just us three watching?
Three is the scariest. The pot doesn't look at me.
Captain Drum took a pot lid from his bag and held it before his face. Yeoni copied him. Yeongnyangi covered his eyes with a paw.
Two spoons of soy, one spoon of sweet. Keep the heart gentle and high the heat.
A small voice, but it had rhythm. Behind his lid, Captain Drum tapped his knees. Yeoni's tail swayed to the beat.
See? All it takes is one lid between us.
You going to tell the whole island to wear lids at noon?
Not a bad idea. A lid festival.
On an evening whose sunset never moved, Yeoni toured the alleys with flyers against their chest. Only pictures on the flyers: a sun, a skewer, a smiling face.
At one corner, a lamp went out. Yeoni stopped. They knew this sequence now.
Cute flyer. Two stars for drawing ability.
Don't rate other people's promotional materials.
The noon concert. Everyone's heard. The crows know too.
...Already?
Rumors travel faster than songs here. Songs are banned; rumors aren't.
The tiger opened its ledger. One line stood empty. Yeoni's name was written at the top.
So here's an offer. I'll lend you applause. At noon, a thousand people below the stage will clap for you.
A thousand?
Enough applause raises the sun too. Even if the singing's clumsy. Guaranteed.
Yeoni looked at the ledger. The empty line glittered. It looked easy. Far too easy.
What's the interest?
Now you ask that too.
Learned at the underground stage. Paid for with Yeoul's voice.
We'll decide later. I'll give you a good rate.
No.
The tiger's tail stopped.
A sun raised on borrowed applause will set when repayment comes. Then this island spends its whole life paying you interest.
Clumsy or not, we'll raise it with real applause. If it won't rise, we'll sing again tomorrow.
...There might not be a tomorrow.
Are you worrying about me?
Business. Lose a customer and the ledger goes empty.
Then I'll just sing well today.
The tiger shut the book, a little louder than usual.
Debts grow if left alone. Even debts you never took. Refusal has a price of its own.
And Yeoni. Don't go up on the roof tonight.
What's that supposed to mean? Warning or threat?
No answer. When the lamp came on again, the alley was empty.
That night, Yeoni could not sleep. They eased open the underground kitchen's hatch and climbed onto the roof. Things they were told not to do always made them curious.
Just one practice. Very quietly.
Looking toward the Sundial Stage, Yeoni hummed. Sol to mi. The notes that had earned ridicule in the courtroom net. Strangely, it felt good.
As the humming ended, one patch of moonless sky grew darker. Wings.
The voice that will raise the stage at noon.
Confiscated.
Wait, sentencing can only happen in court—right, there's no law like that, is there.
The crow opened its beak. A shining thread unwound from Yeoni's throat. Trembling in the shapes of sol and mi, it was drawn into the mask.
Yeoni tried to shout. Breath passed through their throat. Nothing came out.
The crow flew away. Only one pig and a black feather remained on the roof.
Below, the hatch opened. Yeongnyangi was climbing up. Yeoni called to him.
Yeongnyangi. Their mouth unmistakably formed the name. Not a sound came.
